protocol.name: umbriel_global_shortcuts_v1
protocol.description: Private bridge for the GlobalShortcuts portal backend. Application labels are untrusted. Binding new shortcut IDs requires physical approval, or a compositor-issued credential covering the application and shortcut IDs. Credentials must remain private to the backend and compositor.

request.name: create_session
request.description: The application is a nonempty UTF-8 identifier of at most 256 bytes. A bridge client may have 16 live sessions, with 64 compositor-wide. Invalid identifiers and exhausted capacity produce a closed session, without disconnecting the client. Destroy closed objects normally. Destroying the manager does not destroy its sessions.

interface.name: umbriel_global_shortcuts_session_v1
interface.description:
Status values are zero for success, one for cancellation, and two for failure. A bind may be attempted once, including failure or cancellation. Restore may be attempted once, before bind or the first list. Destroying the session cancels pending approval and releases its live chords, while retaining durable approval. Closed sessions accept only failing operations.
Request IDs are scoped to this session and must be unique while pending. Only bind can remain pending. Reusing its ID fails the original bind, cancels its approval, and ignores the duplicate operation. A second bind with a different ID fails without cancelling the pending operation. Cancellation and destruction prevent late approval from issuing a grant.

request.name: restore

description.summary: consume and replace a private approval credential

request.description: A successful restore emits grant before restored. Invalid credentials leave the session unapproved; its one bind may request fresh approval. Restore creates no live bindings. Application labels alone never restore approval. The backend must save the replacement credential before completing the corresponding public request.

request.name: add_shortcut
request.description: Stage at most 128 shortcuts with unique nonempty UTF-8 IDs of at most 256 bytes. Descriptions are UTF-8 of at most 1024 bytes; preferred triggers are UTF-8 of at most 256 bytes, using the shortcuts specification grammar. An empty trigger means absent. Invalid or disallowed preferred triggers leave the shortcut unassigned. Invalid staging fails the next bind. Bind always clears staging. Session and entry limits also bound total staged data and pending operations per client and compositor.

request.name: list

description.summary: list successful bindings without activating them

request.description: Before bind, return only previously successful bindings from a restored grant. After bind, return the current live subset. Shortcut events precede listed, including an empty successful list. Trigger descriptions are human-readable. An unassigned shortcut is omitted from bound results.

request.name: cancel

description.summary: cancel a pending bind by request ID

request.description: A matching pending bind completes once with cancellation status. Unknown and already completed request IDs have no effect.

event.name: changed

description.summary: one entry in a complete replacement snapshot

event.description: Each batch ends with changes_done, even when empty. A removed active binding is deactivated before the replacement snapshot is published.
